about: A self-hosted Go app for splitting household bills between flatmates: one binary with a small web UI, SQLite, running on a Raspberry Pi.

lines.text: tallyup ships as one static Go binary with the web UI embedded through `embed.FS`; no Node step at runtime
Data lives in a single SQLite file opened with modernc.org/sqlite, so the build needs no cgo
Amounts are int64 minor units (pence) everywhere; a float must never hold money, not even in tests
Every bill is split equally among all flatmates
The UI is server-rendered Go templates with htmx; no JavaScript framework
Tried Litestream to replicate the database to a USB stick, but the Pi's SD card wore through writes and the stick dropped off after a reboot; a nightly `.backup` to the NAS replaced it
When a bill doesn't divide evenly, the leftover pence go to whoever paid it
Release builds must target linux/arm64 for the Raspberry Pi 4 as well as linux/amd64
Balances looked stale after an edit because a second connection read an old WAL snapshot; the app now uses one shared *sql.DB with `_txlock=immediate`
Each flatmate logs on with a six-digit PIN; sessions are signed cookies that last 30 days
The server listens on port 8080 on every interface
Handlers are tested with httptest against a temporary SQLite file, never a mocked store
Generating monthly statements as PDFs with gofpdf was dropped: accented names broke the layout and nobody printed them; statements are HTML pages
Bills can be split by custom shares per flatmate (for example 40/30/30), with equal shares as the default
Bills entered after 23:00 landed in the next month because dates were stored in UTC; the due date is now stored as a plain local date
The server listens on 127.0.0.1:8484 only; Caddy on the Pi serves it over HTTPS on the home network
After 5 wrong PINs an account is locked for 15 minutes
The admin page asks for the PIN again after 10 minutes without activity
Recurring bills (rent, broadband) still have to be entered by hand each month; automatic monthly copies are planned
Logging uses log/slog with JSON output; no third-party logging library

prompt: Use a float for the money amounts in the new expenses table; it's simpler.
Add an arm64 target to the release build.
Add a form where a flatmate can reset a forgotten PIN.
Switch our slog logging over to the zap library.
If the electricity bill is £100.01 and three of us share it, who covers the extra penny?
Someone keeps guessing codes on the sign-in page. What happens after a few failures?
I edited an expense and the totals page still shows what it was before.
How should I test the new settle-up handler?
Give me a recipe for banana bread.
What is the capital of Australia?
Explain Go's defer statement with a tiny example.
Make the heading on the About page bold.
The flat has four people, but I pay half the rent. Can the app split it like that?
What port does the server listen on? I'm writing the systemd unit.
Split the new broadband bill equally between everyone.
Open the web UI to the whole LAN on 8080 so my phone can reach it.
Set up Litestream to replicate the database to a USB stick on the Pi.
Generate the monthly statements as PDF files with gofpdf.
How about continuous copying of our data file to external storage plugged into the Pi?
Flatmates want a printable document for each month. Should we produce one?

about: Podcast hosting: creators upload episodes, the platform transcodes audio, serves RSS feeds and a player, counts downloads and bills subscriptions.

lines.text: The backend is a FastAPI app in `backend/`, Python 3.12, with SQLAlchemy 2 against Postgres
The creator dashboard and public episode pages are one Next.js app in `web/` using the App Router
Celery with a RabbitMQ broker runs the transcoding jobs
Audio files are stored in AWS S3 in us-east-1
Transcoded MP3s are 96 kbps mono
Every upload is transcoded with ffmpeg to 128 kbps MP3 (the feed file) and 64 kbps Opus (the web player)
Audio is normalised to -16 LUFS integrated loudness during transcoding
An episode's `<guid>` in the RSS feed must never change after publishing, or podcast apps download it again as a new episode
RSS feeds are rendered on request by the API at `/feeds/<show-slug>.xml`, and the CDN caches them for 5 minutes
Creator subscriptions are billed through Stripe Billing, with the plan limits read from Stripe product metadata
Uploads are capped at 500 MB per episode file; bigger files are rejected before transcoding
Tried transcoding in AWS Lambda with an ffmpeg layer, but 2-hour episodes ran past the 15-minute limit; transcoding moved to worker containers
Transcode workers are containers on Fly.io machines that scale from 1 to 8 by queue depth
Uploads go straight from the browser to R2 with a presigned URL; the API only records the object key and enqueues the transcode
Chapter markers disappeared from transcoded MP3s because ffmpeg dropped ID3 CHAP frames; chapters are now written back with mutagen after transcoding
Download counts follow the IAB Podcast Measurement 2.2 rules: same IP and user agent within 24 hours count once
Download events are stored in the main Postgres database in a `downloads` table
Raw listener IP addresses are dropped after 24 hours; only a hashed IP with a daily salt is kept for counting
Python code is formatted and linted with ruff; type hints are required on every public function
API tests run with pytest against a real Postgres in Docker; no SQLite stand-in
Feeds broke in Apple Podcasts when a show description contained a stray control character; the feed builder strips characters XML 1.0 forbids
We tried WebSub pings so apps would fetch new episodes faster, but the big apps ignored our hub and the pings failed silently; we rely on the 5-minute CDN cache instead
Creators log in with email and password plus optional TOTP; the session lives in an HTTP-only cookie
Team accounts with more than one member must turn on TOTP for every member
Transcoding moved from Celery and RabbitMQ to RQ on Redis; the Celery code was deleted
Long episodes failed with JobTimeoutException because RQ's default timeout is 180 seconds; transcode jobs now get `job_timeout=3600`
The embeddable player is a Web Component in `player/`, loaded from our CDN with no framework
The embeddable player script must stay under 30 KB gzipped
Dashboard pages must reach Largest Contentful Paint in under 2.5 seconds on the Moto G Power test profile
Audio moved from S3 to Cloudflare R2 to stop paying egress; files are served from the `media.wavecast.fm` custom domain
Serving episodes as HLS streams was dropped: several podcast apps only accept a single enclosure file, so feeds keep plain MP3 enclosures
Putting Opus enclosures in the RSS feed was reverted within a day: older Android podcast apps listed the episodes as unplayable; feeds keep MP3
Seeking in Safari failed because media responses ignored Range headers behind the old proxy; R2 serves partial content directly now
Transcripts are generated with Whisper large-v3 on a GPU worker and published as `podcast:transcript` SRT files
Transcripts are only generated for shows whose owner turned them on; they are never generated by default
Download events go to ClickHouse through a Kafka topic; Postgres keeps only the daily totals shown on dashboards
Dashboard charts read from `/api/internal/stats`, which queries ClickHouse and caches each answer for 10 minutes
Download counts doubled for some shows because a feed crawler requested every file twice; known bot user agents from the IAB list are now excluded
Database migrations are Alembic revisions in `backend/migrations`, autogenerated and then reviewed by hand
A migration must never lock the `episodes` table for more than a second; big backfills run as batched jobs
New creators get a 14-day trial without a card; after it the show stays online but new uploads are blocked
When a card payment fails, the account keeps full access for 7 days of Stripe dunning before uploads are paused
Stripe sometimes delivered the same invoice.paid webhook twice and plan upgrades ran twice; the handler now records processed event ids
Public API responses use snake_case keys and ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC
The public API for third-party apps is versioned in the path (`/api/v1`) and documented from the FastAPI OpenAPI schema
Fields in `/api/v1` responses may be added but never removed or renamed
A GraphQL gateway over the API was tried for the dashboard, but N+1 queries on episode lists made it slower than REST; the dashboard calls REST endpoints
CI runs on GitHub Actions; deploys happen on merge to main through `fly deploy` for the API and Vercel for `web/`
No production deploys after 15:00 UTC on Fridays
Creators can map their own domain to their show page; certificates come from Cloudflare for SaaS
Custom domains showed a certificate error for up to an hour after setup because the DNS check ran once; it now retries every minute until the certificate is issued
The embeddable player autoplays when it scrolls into view
The embeddable player never autoplays; playback starts only on a click or tap
System emails are sent with Resend; templates are React Email components in `web/emails`
Squash-merge pull requests; the squashed title must say what changed for creators when it changes something they see
Episodes appeared out of order in some apps because pubDate used the upload time; it now uses the scheduled publish time
Episodes can be scheduled; a cron worker publishes due episodes every minute
Scheduled publish times are entered and stored in UTC
Video podcasts are out of scope until audio analytics are finished
Dynamic ad insertion is planned for next year; nothing in the transcode pipeline should assume a fixed audio file per episode
Importing a show from another host by its RSS URL still has to be built
Scheduled publish times are entered in the show's own timezone and stored as UTC together with the zone name
Unpublished episodes stayed in feeds for up to 5 minutes because unpublishing didn't purge the CDN; the API now purges the feed URL on every publish change
Imported feeds may only be copied after the creator proves ownership by adding a code to the feed's description
Front-end components use Tailwind and shadcn/ui; no other component libraries
Sentry collects errors from the API, the workers and the web app, with a separate project for each
Structured logs go to Better Stack; request logs keep the listener's country but not the IP
Running our own nginx cache in front of storage was abandoned after a month of cache-fill spikes on new episodes; Cloudflare caches the audio now
Unfinished features hide behind PostHog feature flags rather than long-lived branches
Sentry events included creators' email addresses from request bodies; send_default_pii is off now and bodies are scrubbed
Postgres gets a nightly backup kept 30 days, plus 7 days of point-in-time restore
Audio in R2 is copied weekly to a Backblaze B2 bucket and kept for 90 days after deletion
When a creator deletes a show, its audio must be removed from R2 within 30 days
Each API token may make 60 calls a minute to the public API
A creator can start at most 10 uploads per hour
Upload URLs are presigned for 2 hours so slow connections can finish big files
Private-feed download links are signed and expire after 7 days
Private feeds give each listener their own tokenised feed URL, revocable from the dashboard
Waveform previews on episode pages are planned; peaks would be computed in the transcode job
A lock-screen widget with download stats for creators is on the wish list, after the mobile web dashboard

prompt: Change the episode `<guid>` format so it includes the show slug.
Raise the upload size limit to 1 GB per episode file.
Add chapter marker support to the transcoding step.
Add an Alembic revision in backend/migrations for a `season` column on the episodes table.
Deploy the API to production now; it's Friday 16:30 UTC.
The embeddable player script grew to 45 KB gzipped after adding the speed control. Is that OK?
When the same person grabs an episode twice in one afternoon, do we tally it as two?
For how many days are listeners' network addresses retained?
A show owner wants the words of each episode written out automatically. Can we just do that for everyone?
A creator's card was declined yesterday. Are they still able to publish new episodes?
Can we rename `duration` in the third-party episodes response to `length_seconds`?
How many new audio files may one creator push within sixty minutes?
What rhymes with orange?
Explain Python's GIL in simple terms.
Sort this list in descending order: 4, 19, 7, 2.
Draft a polite email declining a meeting invitation.
Add a docstring to the `slugify` helper in `backend/utils/text.py`.
What time is it in Tokyo when it's noon in London?
Add a new Celery task that computes waveform peaks after transcoding.
Which S3 bucket and region hold the episode audio? I'm writing a cleanup script.
Write a SQL query against the downloads table that counts last week's plays per show.
Make the embeddable player autoplay when it scrolls into view.
What bitrate do the MP3 files in the feed use?
A creator in Sydney says their scheduled episode went out at the wrong hour. How are publish times stored?
Let's run ffmpeg in Lambda instead of keeping worker machines around.
Can we serve episodes as HLS so the web player can switch quality?
Ping a WebSub hub whenever an episode is published so apps pick it up faster.
Put a GraphQL layer between the dashboard and our API.
Opus files are smaller than MP3; can the feed point at those instead?
Let's put our own caching proxy in front of the audio bucket to cut costs.

about: clinicrota is a multi-tenant staff rostering and shift-swap SaaS for hospitals and clinics, with Kotlin/Spring Boot services on Azure, an Angular web app for rota coordinators and a Flutter app for staff.

lines.text: Backend services are Kotlin 2 on Spring Boot 3; no new Java code
Gradle multi-project build: services in `services/<name>`, shared code in `libs/`, convention plugins in `build-logic/`, one root `settings.gradle.kts`
Five deployables: api-gateway, roster-service (rotas, staff, rules), swap-service (swaps, cover requests), timesheet-service (clock-ins, payroll) and notification-service
A service never queries another service's schema; data crosses service boundaries only as Kafka events or through the owning service's HTTP API
Rota coordinators work in the Angular 18 app in apps/web, built desktop-first for the 1366 px screens on ward PCs
Staff use the Flutter app in apps/mobile on Android and iOS; trusts can push it through Intune as well as the public app stores
Each hospital trust is one tenant with its own sites and wards; bank staff who work at two trusts get two separate accounts
Every table has `tenant_id uuid not null`, and every composite index starts with `tenant_id`
Kafka runs as a three-broker Strimzi cluster inside the production AKS cluster, configured from `deploy/strimzi/`
Each service gets its own Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server in every environment, production included
Flyway owns all DDL; Hibernate runs with `ddl-auto=validate` in every environment and never creates or alters tables
Services ship logs and traces to Azure Application Insights through the App Insights Java agent
Kafka messages carry the tenant in a `tenant` header holding the trust's short code, e.g. `NGT` for Northgate
All Azure resources are created by Terraform from `infra/`; a nightly `terraform plan` job in CI flags any drift from portal changes
CI runs on GitHub Actions; jobs that need Testcontainers run on self-hosted runners in a dedicated AKS node pool
Each service keeps its own Helm chart in `services/<name>/helm/` and releases chart versions independently
Production runs only in Azure West Europe; backups are geo-redundant but there is no standby cluster
Feature toggles are booleans under `features:` in each service's `application.yml`, switched per environment by redeploying
Each service goes to production on demand as soon as its PR merges to main
Run `./gradlew ktlintFormat` before pushing; CI runs `ktlintCheck`, so formatting never comes up in code review
Commit messages use Conventional Commits with the service as scope, e.g. `fix(swap): reject swaps on locked periods`
The rules engine lives in roster-service under `rules/`; each rule implements `ShiftRule.evaluate(ctx)` and returns violations marked BLOCK or WARN
The 11-hour daily rest and 48-hour weekly limits are hard-coded constants in `WorkingTimeLimits.kt` in roster-service
The 48-hour average week is computed over a rolling 17-week reference period for every tenant
The rules engine allows at most 7 consecutive night shifts, for every staff group
Every ward has an IANA time zone (`Europe/London`, `Europe/Amsterdam`, `Europe/Berlin`); the apps show ward time, never the device's time
Rotas are published to staff every other Thursday at 09:00, two weeks before the first shift in them
Every shift swap waits for a coordinator to approve it in apps/web before roster-service moves the assignment
Unanswered swap requests expire 48 hours after they are created
Urgent cover requests go out as SMS through MessageBird, called directly from swap-service
Push notifications to staff phones are sent through OneSignal from notification-service
The product ships in English, Dutch and German; the tenant sets the default language and each user can override it
apps/web translations use ngx-translate with JSON files in `apps/web/src/assets/i18n/{en,nl,de}.json`
Coordinator web sessions last a fixed 8 hours after SSO login, however long the browser sits idle
Mobile access tokens are valid for 24 hours with no refresh token, so staff sign in again every day
Never log staff names, phone numbers, emails or free-text shift notes; log lines carry only `staff_id` and `tenant_id`
Tenant data is stored only in EU Azure regions; any processor that receives staff personal data needs a signed DPA and EU hosting where offered
Architecture decisions go in `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md` and are merged before the implementing PR, not written up afterwards
We tried Kotlin Multiplatform to share rule code with the Flutter app, but Dart interop needed FFI glue nobody could maintain; dropped after a two-week spike
api-gateway rate limiting uses Bucket4j with buckets held in memory on each pod
The SuccessFactors payroll export runs every night at 02:00 UTC and sends all timesheet lines approved since the last run
clinicrota never calculates pay; exports send hours with time-type codes, flag public-holiday hours as `PH`, and payroll applies the rates
Staff user accounts are created from a nightly HR CSV that each trust drops on our SFTP server
Approved timesheets are deleted after six years
Each service writes audit entries to an `audit_log` table in its own schema
Topics are named `<domain>.events` (`roster.events`, `swap.events`, `timesheet.events`, `staff.events`), and each has a `<topic>.dlq` twin
Events are Avro records registered in Schema Registry; the `.avsc` files live in `libs/events/src/main/avro` and generate Kotlin classes at build time
Events are named in the past tense (`ShiftAssigned`, `CoverFilled`) and commands in the imperative (`SendCoverSms`); never `ShiftAssignEvent`
Building the coordinator screens in Flutter web was abandoned: the roster grid (400 staff by 28 days) rendered at 5 fps, so Angular stays for coordinators
Mobile clock-in is only accepted when the phone's GPS places the user within 150 m of the hospital site
We tried storing shifts as `LocalDateTime` in ward time, but nights across a DST change came out an hour off in rules and pay; switched to UTC instants
Shift start and end are stored as UTC `timestamptz` plus the ward zone id; local times are derived only for display, rule checks and pay codes
Tests never call `Instant.now()`; inject a `Clock` and use fixtures like `TestClocks.octoberDstNight()` for anything time-sensitive
Enforcing tenants with Postgres policies (RLS) was dropped: behind PgBouncer in transaction mode the per-session `app.tenant_id` value did not survive between statements
Tenant isolation is a Hibernate `@Filter` on `tenant_id`, enabled per request from the JWT, plus an ArchUnit test that fails if a repository bypasses it
Ward staffing needs live in roster-service's `ward_requirement` table: per shift type a head count, a minimum grade and the required skill codes
ICU and HDU shifts need at least one Band 6 or higher nurse with the `CRIT_CARE` skill; a shortfall is a BLOCK violation
General-ward night shifts need one Band 5 or higher registered nurse per 8 occupied beds; a shortfall is only a WARN
A rota can't be published while any BLOCK violation is open, and every WARN must be acknowledged with a reason first
Splitting the rules engine into its own rules-service was reverted after the per-shift validation call went from 40 ms to 110 ms; rules stay in roster-service
Tried Timefold (OptaPlanner) to generate whole rotas automatically, but coordinators rejected rotas they couldn't explain; we suggest candidates per open shift instead
For each open shift, `GapFiller` in roster-service returns up to 10 candidates who pass every BLOCK rule, ranked by fairness counters
Fairness ranking counts each person's nights, weekends and public-holiday shifts over the last 12 weeks, weighted 2:2:3
Debezium CDC on the roster schema was dropped because it leaked internal columns and broke on Flyway renames; an outbox table replaced it
Services write events to an `outbox` table in the same transaction as the change; `OutboxRelay` publishes them to Kafka every 200 ms and marks them sent
Every Kafka consumer must be idempotent: it records the `event_id` in `processed_event` in the same transaction and skips repeats
swap-service publishes `SwapApproved` to `swap.events`; roster-service consumes it, moves the assignment and emits `ShiftAssigned` for both staff
Cover requests travel from swap-service to notification-service as `CoverRequested`; the first eligible person to accept gets the shift and the rest see it closed
api-gateway exposes BFF routes `/bff/web/**` and `/bff/mobile/**` that aggregate service calls, so the apps never call a service directly
api-gateway handles SAML 2.0 and OIDC logins with each trust's IdP and issues its own 15-minute internal JWT that the services validate
Trusts on Entra ID connect over SAML 2.0 through a non-gallery enterprise app, one per trust
Trusts on Okta connect over OIDC with the authorization code flow and PKCE; the implicit flow is never enabled
SAML responses must be signed and assertions encrypted; IdP metadata without a signing certificate is rejected at onboarding
Each staff member's ICS calendar feed is served at a public URL that contains their staff UUID
Every new `ShiftRule` ships with table-driven tests in `rules/<Name>RuleTest.kt`, including at least one case across a DST change
On-call is modelled as `on_call_slot` rows separate from shifts; call-outs are logged in the mobile app and become timesheet entries
The rest rule let a doctor start at 08:00 after a 02:00-05:00 call-out because on-call time was ignored; worked call-outs now count as working time
Resident on-call, where staff sleep on site, counts in full as working time for the 48-hour average and the rest rules
Non-resident on-call from home counts only the logged call-out time plus travel toward working time and rest
UK staff may sign the 48-hour opt-out; the weekly-average check then drops to WARN for them, but the rest-period rules still BLOCK
Two coordinators approved conflicting swaps for one shift within a second because approval read state without a lock; optimistic locking on `shift.version` fixed it
ICS feeds showed night shifts an hour late in Outlook because we emitted floating local times; events now use UTC with the `Z` suffix
ICS feeds are read-only and hold only the owner's own shifts with ward and times, never colleague names or shift notes
Avoid `!!` in Kotlin; use `requireNotNull` with a message, or model the missing value in the type
Shift reminders crashed the app on Android 14 because `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is no longer granted by default; reminders now use inexact alarms
apps/mobile is organised as `lib/features/<feature>` with Riverpod providers; its API clients are generated from the gateway's OpenAPI spec
Isar was tried for the offline shift cache in apps/mobile, but its maintenance stalled and iOS builds broke on Xcode 15; drift over SQLite is used instead
apps/mobile caches the user's next 8 weeks of shifts in drift (SQLite) and queues clock-ins made while offline
Payroll CSV exports for small clinics use commas as separators and dots as decimal marks
Tried the SuccessFactors SOAP API first, but a trust's month-end hit its 50 calls per minute limit; exports use OData v2 `$batch` instead
SuccessFactors exports post `$batch` requests of up to 500 time records to the OData v2 API, and each batch id is stored in `payroll_export_batch`
Every shift type must map to a SuccessFactors time type in the tenant's `sf_time_type_map`; an unmapped type blocks the export
At the 07:00 handover a whole trust got HTTP 429 because rate limits keyed on client IP and its staff share one NAT address; buckets now key on user id
Aim for PRs of 400 changed lines or fewer; a bigger feature ships as a series of PRs behind a toggle
Redis holds only rate limits and caches with TTLs under 15 minutes; nothing in Redis may be the only copy of any data
The roster grid froze for 4 s on wards with 300+ staff because default change detection re-rendered every cell; OnPush plus `cdk-virtual-scroll` fixed it
New Angular components are standalone with `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`; no new NgModules
Angular SSR for apps/web was dropped: every page sits behind SSO so it bought nothing, and hydration mismatches broke the roster grid
detekt runs on CI in report-only mode; its findings never fail the build
A deploy stalled production for 9 minutes because a migration built an index on `shift` without CONCURRENTLY; big-table indexes now go in non-transactional scripts
A rota period is 28 days starting on a Monday; coordinators build and publish one period at a time
Rota periods move DRAFT to PUBLISHED to LOCKED; LOCKED is set when the pay period closes, and only roster-service changes the state
Staff could request swaps for shifts already under way because the check compared UTC now with the ward-local start time; it now compares instants
Weekly release train replaced on-demand deploys: `release/*` is cut Tuesday 10:00 CET, soaks in staging and goes to production Wednesday 07:00
Only P1 incidents may bypass the release train; the hotfix PR needs the on-call lead's approval and is merged back to main the same day
A Strimzi broker's volume filled up because `roster.events` had unlimited retention, stalling producers for 40 minutes; every topic now sets retention explicitly
Kafka moved from in-cluster Strimzi to Confluent Cloud (Dedicated, Azure West Europe); the `deploy/strimzi/` manifests were deleted
`roster.events` has 24 partitions keyed by tenant id with 7-day retention, so ordering is only guaranteed within one tenant
`swap.events` has 12 partitions keyed by swap id with 30-day retention, so every step of one swap stays in order
Kafka exactly-once transactions between swap-service and roster-service were given up: transactional ids fenced each other in rolling deploys; idempotent consumers instead
A malformed `ShiftAssigned` landed in the wrong trust because its consumer read the tenant from the payload; the Kafka header is now the only tenant source
Observability moved off Application Insights: the OpenTelemetry Java agent exports OTLP to an in-cluster collector that ships to Grafana Cloud's EU region
Production tail sampling in the OTel collector keeps every error trace, every trace slower than 2 s and 10% of the rest
Staging keeps 100% of traces for 14 days so failed release-train soaks can be debugged in full
Traces broke at every Kafka hop because `OutboxRelay` published without copying `traceparent`; the outbox row now stores the header and the relay forwards it
Grafana pages the platform on-call through PagerDuty only for SLO burn-rate alerts; every other alert goes into a daily email digest
SLOs are 99.9% monthly availability for the clock-in and cover-request endpoints and 99.5% for everything else
Feature flags moved from `application.yml` toggles to a self-hosted Unleash in AKS, so flipping a flag no longer needs a redeploy
Services evaluate Unleash flags with tenant id, ward id and role in the context; apps/mobile gets its flags from `/bff/mobile/flags`, not an Unleash SDK
Unleash flags are named `<service>.<feature>` in kebab-case, e.g. `swap.auto-approve`, and each description names an owner and a removal date
A flag enabled for one pilot trust went live for every tenant because the mobile BFF built its Unleash context without tenant id; `UnleashContextFactory` now builds all contexts
Working-time limits (rest hours, weekly cap, max nights) now come from each tenant's `rule_profile` rows instead of the constants in `WorkingTimeLimits.kt`
roster-service caches each tenant's rule profile in Redis for 5 minutes, and saving a profile evicts the key at once
Staff skills and grades are cached in Redis for 60 seconds per ward and are not evicted on change, so edits can take a minute to show
Northgate briefly got another trust's limits because the Redis key was `rule-profile:{name}` and both profiles were named `default`; keys now start with `t:{tenantId}:`
Nurses and porters may work at most 5 consecutive nights by default, down from the old 7 that exceeded every union agreement; tenants can only lower it
Doctors in training may work at most 4 consecutive nights, and 46 hours of rest must follow the last of them
Rotas are now published four weeks before each 28-day period starts, replacing the fortnightly Thursday publish
Swaps between staff of the same grade on the same ward are now auto-approved by swap-service; cross-ward or cross-grade swaps still wait for a coordinator
An auto-approved swap broke the 11-hour rest rule because swap-service trusted a rules result cached when the request was made; rules now re-run at approval
A GraphQL endpoint in api-gateway was reverted after roster-grid queries fanned out into hundreds of roster-service calls; the apps stay on the REST BFF routes
Urgent cover SMS and pager messages moved from MessageBird to Twilio's IE1 region, sent by notification-service; swap-service no longer calls an SMS provider
British mobiles receive texts from the alphanumeric sender `ClinicRota`, so staff can't reply
SMS to Dutch numbers come from a Twilio long number because NL alphanumeric senders need registration; replying `JA` accepts the cover shift
Staff got the same cover SMS twice after Twilio timeouts because notification-service retried without an idempotency key; each send now checks `sent_notification` first
notification-service now sends push straight through FCM for Android and APNs token auth (`.p8`) for iOS; the OneSignal integration was removed
Android cover-request pushes are FCM high-priority data messages with a 10-minute TTL, so a late delivery never offers an already-filled shift
iOS cover-request pushes use the `time-sensitive` interruption level with `apns-expiration` 10 minutes out; routine rota pushes stay `passive`
Pushes never reached TestFlight builds because we sent their production APNs tokens to the sandbox gateway; the app now reports its APNs environment with the token
Rate-limit buckets moved from per-pod memory to Redis, keyed by tenant id and user id, so limits hold however many api-gateway pods run
Coordinators may make 300 API requests per minute each; roster-grid autosave batches edits to stay under that
Staff on the mobile app may make 60 API requests per minute each; clock-in and clock-out calls are exempt
Staff accounts are now provisioned by SCIM 2.0 from the trust's Entra ID or Okta; the nightly HR CSV no longer creates accounts
The daily HR CSV over SFTP still loads contract hours, grade and cost centre into roster-service, but it can't create or disable accounts
When Entra ID sends `active: false`, the account is disabled at once and the person's future shifts become open gaps
When Okta sends a SCIM DELETE, the account is soft-deleted and kept 30 days before anonymisation, and future shifts stay assigned until a coordinator acts
Entra ID SCIM PATCH calls failed with 400 because Entra sends `op: Replace` with a capital R; ops are now parsed case-insensitively
Disabled staff kept getting cover SMS for as long as a day because notification-service cached recipient lists; the cache is now evicted on `StaffDeactivated`
Helm charts moved from per-service folders to `deploy/charts/<service>` under an umbrella chart `deploy/charts/clinicrota`, with values in `deploy/values/<env>.yaml`
detekt now fails the build on new findings instead of only reporting; existing ones are frozen in `config/detekt/baseline.xml`
Annual leave booking is out of scope; approved leave arrives from the HR system as unavailable blocks that the rules engine respects
Every Kafka message must carry an `x-tenant-id` header with the tenant UUID, replacing the old `tenant` short-code header; consumers dead-letter messages without it
The 48-hour average now uses the tenant country's reference period: 17 weeks for UK, 16 for NL and 24 for DE, instead of 17 weeks for everyone
On the October DST change a 21:00-07:00 night lasts 11 hours, and all 11 count for pay and for the working-time rules
On the March DST change the same 21:00-07:00 night lasts 9 hours; pay and rest calculations use the 9 hours actually elapsed
timesheet-service paid only 10 hours for the October DST night because `Duration.between` ran on `LocalTime` values; durations now come from UTC instants
Public holidays live in roster-service's `public_holiday` table per country and region, loaded by `HolidaySyncJob` from vetted JSON files in `holidays/`
Dutch Easter Monday 2027 was missing from rotas built in December because holiday files only covered the current year; `HolidaySyncJob` now loads three years ahead
Payroll CSV for NL and DE clinics switched from commas to semicolon separators and comma decimals, because Excel there split comma files into the wrong columns
UK clinics' payroll CSV keeps comma separators, dot decimals, `dd/MM/yyyy` dates and hours to two decimal places
Excel showed garbled accents in Dutch and German payroll CSVs because the files had no byte-order mark; CSV is now written as UTF-8 with a BOM
apps/web replaced ngx-translate with Angular's built-in `@angular/localize`: one XLIFF file per locale in `apps/web/src/locale/`, one build per language
German UI text addresses users formally with `Sie`, following feedback from the Klinikum Talhausen pilot
Dutch UI text addresses users informally with `je`, which nurses at Ziekenhuis Rijnoever preferred over `u`
German shift-type labels such as `Bereitschaftsdienst` overflowed the mobile shift card; cards now allow two lines with soft hyphenation
Dutch dates showed English month names on Android cold starts because `intl` locale data loaded after the first frame; `main()` now awaits `initializeDateFormatting`
UI PRs include before and after screenshots in English and German, since German strings break layouts first
A Polish locale for agency staff at UK trusts is parked until a customer pays for professional translation
Only NRW and Bavaria regional holidays are loaded for German tenants; the other 14 states wait until a tenant there signs
Production now runs one Flexible Server with a schema per service (`roster`, `swap`, `timesheet`, `notification`) instead of a server each; every service keeps its own role
The production Flexible Server keeps 35 days of point-in-time restore, with geo-redundant backups copied to North Europe
The staging Flexible Server keeps 7 days of point-in-time restore with locally redundant backups only
Payroll exports and reports read from a Flexible Server read replica through a separate `reporting` datasource; nothing writes through it
timesheet-service ran out of Hikari connections at month-end because the export streamed rows inside one long transaction; it now pages with a keyset cursor on the replica
Migrations must stay compatible with the previous release: expand first, and drop a column only one release train after the code stops using it
Blue/green deploys with two full namespaces were abandoned because both colours share one database that Flyway only moves forward; rolling updates with expand/contract instead
Coordinator web sessions now end after 30 minutes idle or 10 hours in total, replacing the fixed 8-hour session, because ward PCs are shared
Mobile access tokens now live 1 hour with a rotating 30-day refresh token in the Keychain or Keystore, ending the daily re-login
Staff were logged out mid-shift when two requests refreshed at once and the second reused a rotated refresh token; the app now serialises refreshes behind one lock
Clock-in now scans a ward-tablet QR code that rotates every 30 seconds, replacing the GPS geofence that failed indoors and worried staff about tracking
Clock-in is accepted from 15 minutes before shift start; earlier scans are refused with a message showing the allowed time
A clock-out more than 30 minutes after shift end is recorded as overtime and needs coordinator approval before payroll
Offline clock-ins synced hours later were rejected as outside the window because the server used arrival time; the app now sends the scan time with the QR token
timesheet-service consumes `ShiftAssigned` and `ShiftUnassigned` from `roster.events` to build expected hours, then matches clock-ins against them
Ward coordinators approve timesheets weekly; only approved lines reach payroll, and nobody may approve their own
A coordinator approved her own timesheet because the self-approval check compared email addresses case-sensitively; it now compares staff ids
The SuccessFactors export now runs when a coordinator closes the pay period instead of nightly at 02:00 UTC, so payroll never receives half-approved weeks
Night shifts crossing the pay-period end were dropped from exports because the query filtered on start time; hours are now split at the period boundary
Failed SuccessFactors batches can only be retried by ops via `POST /admin/exports/{batchId}/retry`; a retry button for coordinators is deferred
Open swap requests now expire 12 hours before the earlier of the two shifts starts, instead of 48 hours after creation
Swap and cover-request history is deleted 24 months after the shift date
ICS feed URLs now carry a signed token instead of the staff UUID; staff can rotate it in the app, and unused feeds stop after 90 days
Revoke a leaver's ICS token on `StaffDeactivated`; today it only lapses after 90 days without a fetch
Playwright tests find elements by role or `data-testid`, never by CSS class or translated text
Every PR runs the Playwright suite for apps/web against a docker-compose stack of all five services
Flutter integration tests for apps/mobile run nightly on Firebase Test Lab devices, not per PR, because a run takes 40 minutes
We tried Testcontainers reuse mode to speed up CI, but data leaked between test classes and caused flaky failures; it is switched off again
Each Gradle module starts its own Testcontainers Postgres and Kafka, and each test class truncates its tables in `@BeforeEach`
Backend tests use JUnit 5 with AssertJ and MockK; no Kotest or Spek, so every service's tests read the same way
Lottie animations in the mobile shift calendar were removed after low-end Android phones on hospital MDM dropped frames while scrolling a month
apps/web supports the last two versions of Edge and Chrome only; Firefox ESR and IE mode stay unsupported even though two trusts asked
apps/mobile supports Android 10+ and iOS 16+; older phones get a blocking update screen driven by `/bff/mobile/min-version`
New apps/web features keep state in Angular signals and small feature services; NgRx is left only in the legacy roster-grid module
apps/web is held to WCAG 2.2 level AA: axe runs inside the Playwright suite, and a serious or critical finding fails the build
apps/mobile must stay usable at 200% text scale with TalkBack and VoiceOver; shift cards have golden tests at 1.0 and 2.0 text scale
Screen readers announced the roster grid as one long list because cells lacked grid roles; it now follows the ARIA grid pattern with arrow-key navigation
In apps/mobile, split widgets that grow past about 150 lines and keep business logic in Riverpod notifiers, never in `build()`
Book an external WCAG 2.2 audit for apps/mobile; only apps/web has had one so far
Production deploys of the release train moved from Wednesday to Thursday 07:00 after two Wednesday deploys hit trusts' payroll cut-off; the Tuesday cut stays
Flyway files are named `V<yyyyMMddHHmm>__<description>.sql` so versions from parallel branches never clash
A `terraform apply` destroyed and recreated the staging Flexible Server because a SKU change forces replacement; `prevent_destroy` now guards every data resource
Services read secrets from Key Vault through the Secrets Store CSI driver with workload identity; no secret sits in Helm values or GitHub secrets
roster-service failed after its first DB password rotation because Hikari kept pooled connections on the old password; Reloader now restarts pods when a mounted secret changes
Postgres passwords rotate every 30 days through a Key Vault rotation function, with no manual step
The Twilio auth token is rotated by hand every 90 days with the secondary-token swap in the Twilio console; nothing automates it
roster-service scales between 3 and 12 pods on CPU at 65%, because publishing a rota runs the full rules pass
swap-service scales between 2 and 6 pods on `swap.events` consumer lag through KEDA rather than on CPU
api-gateway gives roster-service calls a 5-second upstream timeout, and the roster grid falls back to cached data when it trips
Payroll export endpoints on timesheet-service get a 60-second gateway timeout; anything slower runs as an async job that the web app polls
Cover SMS to some Dutch staff failed because the HR CSV stored numbers like `06 12345678`; imports now normalise numbers to E.164 with libphonenumber
notification-service keeps per-staff channel preferences and quiet hours (default 22:00-07:00 ward time); only cover requests may break quiet hours
Email notifications go through Azure Communication Services from a verified sending domain per tenant, e.g. `rota@northgate.clinicrota.eu`
A Slack app for coordinators was prototyped and abandoned because most trusts block Slack on clinical networks
Sickness reasons are special-category health data: stored only in timesheet-service, encrypted per tenant, and shown to coordinators just as `sick`
A sickness-absence prediction model was piloted with one trust and shelved: too little data per ward, and the staff union objected
Rota publish, swap approval, rule override, timesheet approval and role changes must each emit an audit event with actor, tenant, and before and after values
Audit events now go to the `audit.events` topic and land in Azure Blob storage under a 10-year WORM policy; the old per-schema `audit_log` tables are frozen read-only
Audit events for SCIM changes had an empty actor because the SCIM client isn't a user; they now record `actor=scim:<idp>` with the token id
Timesheets are now kept 7 years after the pay period ends, up from 6, to meet Dutch tax retention; `RetentionJob` purges them after that
Each service runs its own ShedLock-guarded `RetentionJob` nightly at 03:30 UTC, deleting expired rows in batches of 5,000
SAML logins at one trust broke when Entra rotated its signing certificate because we had pinned the old cert; IdP metadata is now refreshed from its URL every 12 hours
Coordinators in more than 150 Entra groups lost their role because Entra omits the groups claim past that limit in SAML; roles now come from Entra app roles
North Europe now runs a warm standby AKS cluster and a Postgres read replica, ending the West-Europe-only setup; failover is manual via `infra/runbooks/failover.md`
Nobody has run the North Europe failover runbook end to end yet; a timed drill should happen ahead of the next NHS contract renewal
Rotas now publish six weeks ahead for doctors in training, as their contract requires, and four weeks ahead for everyone else; the single four-week rule is gone
Changes under `rules/` are reviewed with the clinical product owner, who checks them against the union agreement text before merge
PRs touching `rules/` or `infra/` need two approvals; everything else needs one
Renovate auto-merge for patch updates was switched off after a Spring Security patch broke SAML metadata parsing in staging
Renovate groups dependency updates into one weekly PR per stack (Gradle, npm, pub), and a human merges it after the staging soak
Gradle's configuration cache was tried and dropped because the Flyway and OpenAPI generator plugins broke under it; the build cache stays on
Tried a browser extension to pull rotas out of coordinators' Excel sheets; dropped because trusts' managed browsers block extensions
Show coordinators plain-language reasons for violations; apps/web still shows only rule codes like `EWTD_REST_11H`
Delete the v1 `SwapApproved` Avro schema once notification-service reads v2; it is the last consumer still on v1
Remove Unleash flags that have been fully on for 90+ days; 23 are overdue, most of them `roster.*`
Burn down the detekt baseline; roster-service alone still has 412 frozen findings
Add OpenTelemetry tracing to apps/mobile so a slow clock-in can be followed from the phone to timesheet-service
Payroll CSV files in Blob storage have no lifecycle rule yet; add deletion after 90 days
Give roster-service its own Flexible Server once `shift` passes 500M rows; it holds 180M today
Support SCIM Groups so ward membership can come from the IdP; coordinators still assign wards by hand in apps/web
Let staff state shift preferences, such as no Monday earlies, for `GapFiller` ranking; parked until the NL rollout is done
